brief.headline: KKR Agreed to Sell Railcar Lessor Infinity Transportation to Ares for About $2.9 Billion
bullets: M&A & Buyouts: KKR has agreed to sell Infinity Transportation, a full-service railcar and intermodal equipment lessor.
People & Leadership: Macquarie Asset Management has hired Linso Pals from Blackstone to head up credit within its client solutions group.
Family Offices & Wealth: The J.P. Morgan subsidiary now offers managed and custom model portfolios, plus equity SMAs, in a UMA for RIAs.
AI & Technology: On Inside Blackstone, host Christine Anderson sits down with Moderna President Dr. Stephen Hoge.
Family Offices & Wealth: Jim Dickson's firm backs the Las Vegas-based Truing Capital, formerly affiliated with UBS, as it pursues an ambitious $50 billion growth target over the next two years.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,712.57 (up 0.3% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 18.4, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.15% (up 6 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.33 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.29%, near long-run norms (down 2 bps on the prior reading).

items.title: SEC, FSA Hold Autumn Financial Regulatory Dialogue
items.takeaway: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Financial Services Agency of Japan (FSA) convened the Autumn SEC-FSA Financial Regulatory Dialogue in Tokyo on Oct. 19.
items.whyItMatters: Meetings like this rarely change rules on their own, but they show what regulators are prioritising, which is often where new rules come from.
items.marketContext: The VIX is 18.4, a normal-volatility reading and high-yield credit spreads are 3.29%, near long-run norms (down 2 bps on the prior reading). Overall risk appetite is healthy. (FRED data as of Oct 20.)

beginnerNote.explanation: An individual or entity that meets SEC wealth or income tests and is therefore allowed to invest in most private funds.

items.title: Bull markets tend to peak with a whimper, not a bang — but a 15% correction for the S&P 500 may be next
items.takeaway: Unlike bear-market bottoms, which typically end with a spasm of despair as traders throw in the towel, bull-market tops are far more gradual and less dramatic.
items.whyItMatters: A lasting selloff in stocks would cut the value of private companies priced against them and make IPOs harder, so watch whether it spreads.

beginnerNote.explanation: The VIX measures how much the stock market expects prices to swing over the next month. Above about 20 signals nervousness; below about 15 signals calm.

items.title: Ares warns Australian private credit faces further stress as rates hit 4.6%
items.takeaway: Ares Management has warned that rising interest rates could intensify pressure on Australia's AUD$200bn private credit market, particularly among lenders exposed to the country's struggling property sector, according to a report by Bloomberg.
items.whyItMatters: Signs of strain in private credit are an early warning for its investors: more defaults or deferred interest would cut income and push down the value of the loans.
items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 3.29%, near long-run norms (down 2 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Oct 20.)

beginnerNote.explanation: Loans made by investment funds rather than banks, usually to mid-sized companies. They often pay higher, floating interest rates.

items.title: German insurers’ private credit allocations set to rise, says Moody’s
items.takeaway: German insurers are expected to increase their private credit allocations despite mounting concerns over liquidity and asset valuations, according to a Moody's Ratings report covered by Reinsurance News.
items.whyItMatters: Moody’s view on private credit is a useful benchmark from someone close to the market, but it is a forecast to weigh against your own, not a guarantee.
